newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to seek nuclear plant bids next week - agency.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to seek nuclear plant bids next week - agency.

text.p: Turkey is expected to seek bids next week for the country's first nuclear power plant, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The plant is to be built near the southern Turkish coastal town of Mersin, close to the village of Akkuyu and is expected to cost about $1.5 billion.
Anatolian said French, United States, Canadian and Japanese companies are conducting preliminary talks with the Turkish energy ministry on the project.
It said the bids are expected to be evaluated by June 1997 and a company or consortium selected for the project by July at the latest.
Construction of the plant is planned to begin towards the end of 1997 and to be completed within around six to seven years, it said.
The plant will be built either as a single unit with a capacity of 1,200 .
MegaWatts (MW) or two equal units each having a capacity of 600 MW, energy minister Recai Kutan said previously.

Industry analysts have said firms interested in the project included France's Framatome, U.S. ABB Combustion Engineering, Westinghouse, Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC), Kvaerner John Brown, Germany's Siemens and some local bidders.
